name: Barcelona
tagline: Mediterranean Cosmopolitan Living on a FIRE Budget
description: Barcelona offers an unmatched blend of beach, culture, architecture, and gastronomy that few cities can rival. While pricier than Eastern or Southern European alternatives, Spain's non-lucrative visa and Beckham Law tax regime make it viable for FIRE retirees who want world-class urban living with a Mediterranean soul.

quickFacts.visa: Non-Lucrative Visa (no work allowed, must show sufficient funds). Beckham Law may reduce taxes for new residents. Path to residency and citizenship.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Safe — standard big-city precautions for pickpocketing in tourist zones
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Barcelona-El Prat Airport (BCN) — 25 min from city center
quickFacts.climate: Mediterranean with mild winters (10-15°C) and hot summers (25-32°C). 2,500+ hours of sunshine per year.

housing.description: Room in a shared flat, Sants / Nou Barris / outer Gràcia

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with the occasional menú del día lunch or evening tapas

healthcare.description: Compliant NLV private policy, no copays, Spanish insurer (Adeslas/ASISA)

entertainment.description: Free Barceloneta beach days, Montjuïc sunsets, and Gothic Quarter wandering

1M.lifestyle: A frugal-but-livable Barcelona base — a room in a shared flat in Sants, Nou Barris, or the Gràcia fringe, home cooking as the default with the occasional menú del día or evening tapas as the treat. Movement is by subsidized T-usual pass and Bicing bike-share, and compliant NLV private cover is carried from day one. Barcelona is not cheap, so this tier trades space for location — but Barceloneta beach, Montjuïc, and the Gothic Quarter cost nothing.

housing.description: Studio or small 1BR in a good non-prime barrio, Sant Antoni / Poblenou / Gràcia

dining.description: Dining out several times a week at neighborhood tapas bars and vermouth spots

healthcare.description: Mid-tier no-copay private plan, wider network (Sanitas/DKV)

entertainment.description: Concerts, FC Barcelona matches, and weekend Costa Brava outings

2M.lifestyle: A studio or small one-bedroom in a good non-prime barrio such as Sant Antoni, Poblenou, or Gràcia. Dining out several times a week at neighborhood tapas bars and vermouth spots, comprehensive private cover, and a weekend rental car for the Costa Brava or Penedès wine country. Everyday life is comfortable and the bill rarely needs a second thought.

dining.description: Regular meals at the city's celebrated restaurants

healthcare.description: Comprehensive private plan, broad hospital network, fast specialist access

entertainment.description: Cultural memberships, Penedès wine trips, and a fuller events calendar

3M.lifestyle: A furnished one-bedroom in desirable, central Eixample, steps from cafés and the metro. Regular meals at the city's celebrated restaurants, a broad-network private plan with fast specialist access, a leased car for weekend escapes, and several European trips a year. Genuinely affluent daily life in one of Barcelona's best districts.

healthcare.description: Premium private cover or entry-level international plan

transportation.description: Add a leased/luxury car (and driver at 10M)

entertainment.description: Premium cultural experiences, beach-club access, and sailing weekends

5M.lifestyle: A renovated, high-spec apartment at a prime-central address with building amenities. Near-daily dining at top restaurants, premium private health cover, regular housekeeping, and a leased luxury car layered on top of transit. Barcelona's real costs are still felt at this level, but practical constraints are few.

housing.description: Luxury 1–2BR, Passeig de Gràcia / Pedralbes prime

dining.description: Private-chef-level dining and the finest Catalan tables

transportation.description: Add a leased/luxury car (and driver at 10M)

entertainment.description: Art, private charters, and premium cultural-and-social life

10M.lifestyle: A luxury residence on Passeig de Gràcia or in leafy Pedralbes. Private-chef-level dining and the finest tables in the city, top-tier international health cover, a chauffeured car on top of transit, full household help, and a generous travel-and-culture budget. Barcelona is no Zurich-scale price outlier, so even uncapped luxury here settles near $10k/mo.
